verified: The Decoder reports that Washington is tightening chip export controls so that data centers in third countries such as Singapore and Malaysia will soon need a US license to buy Nvidia chips, closing a route Chinese firms used to rent cloud compute abroad, and that a Reuters investigation described China offsetting its hardware shortage by distilling US AI models. US officials say they distinguish legitimate distillation from large-scale extraction they characterize as intellectual property theft (tool-3-1).
unconfirmed: The article gives no rule text, agency, license criteria or effective date, so the timing and scope of the licensing requirement rest on secondary reporting. The "industrial-scale" distillation claim is attributed to the Reuters investigation and US officials rather than independent measurement, with US intelligence reportedly naming DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot AI and three other firms (tool-3-2) — an accusation China's Commerce Ministry rejects and has threatened to counter (tool-3-3). No figures quantifying how much Chinese model capability derives from US outputs are provided.

verified: 据 The Decoder 援引路透社调查报道，美国正准备要求新加坡、马来西亚等第三国的数据中心在购买英伟达芯片前取得美国许可证，以堵住中国企业租用海外算力的渠道；美国官员表示，会区分合法的模型蒸馏与大规模型号提取（即被指为知识产权窃取的行为），中国商务部已否认相关指控并警告将采取反制措施（tool-3-1、tool-3-3）。
unconfirmed: 新规的具体条文、生效日期、许可证审批标准和覆盖的芯片型号均未见官方文件，报道本身也未给出这些细节；“工业规模蒸馏”目前只是美方指控，据一家媒体报道，美国情报机构点名了 DeepSeek、阿里巴巴、Moonshot AI 等六家中国企业，但这些企业是否认罪、蒸馏规模有多大，都没有独立测量或司法结论支持，中方则明确拒绝该指控（tool-3-2、tool-3-3）。

titles.en: US to require licenses for Nvidia chips in third countries; China distills US models
titles.zh: 美国拟限第三国购 Nvidia 芯片，中国以模型蒸馏补算力
